source_text: Ὅτι δεῖ τοὺς φωτιζομένους τὴν πίστιν ἐκμανθάνειν, καὶ τῇ πέμπτῃ της ἑβδομάδος ἀπαγγέλειν τῷ ἐπισκόπῳ ἢ τοῖς πρεσβυτέροις.
thought_title: Catechumens must learn and recite the creed
orientation: The council is legislating baptismal preparation, just after limiting reception into baptism to before the last two weeks of Lent.
pass_a_gloss: That [it is] necessary [for] the [ones] being enlightened the faith to learn thoroughly, and on the fifth [day] of the week to report to the bishop or to the elders.

choices.why: The brief's glossary mandates this rendering for candidates for baptism.
The compound verb conveys intensive learning, not mere acquaintance.
The verb means to declare or report back, fitting a formal recitation to clergy.

choices.english: on the fifth day of the week
choices.why: Literal rendering of the Greek ordinal and genitive construction, preserving the weekday reference.

pass_b_english: Those being baptized must learn the faith thoroughly, and on the fifth day of the week they are to report to the bishop or to the presbyters.

last_rejected.quote: they are to report to the bishop or to the presbyters
last_rejected.source_quote: τὴν πίστιν ἐκμανθάνειν, καὶ τῇ πέμπτῃ της ἑβδομάδος ἀπαγγέλειν τῷ ἐπισκόπῳ ἢ τοῖς πρεσβυτέροις
last_rejected.why: ἀπαγγέλειν here means recite the faith already learned, not merely present themselves or make a report.
last_rejected.fix: Those being baptized must learn the faith thoroughly and, on the fifth day of the week, recite it to the bishop or the presbyters.
last_rejected.ruling: ἀπαγγέλλειν means to report/announce; 'report to the bishop' is within range. Context (ἐκμανθάνειν) implies recitation, but 'report' is acceptable, not a major meaning change.
